Agricultural economics is an applied field of economics concerned with the application of economic theory in optimizing the production and distribution of food and fiber products. 
Agricultural economics began as a branch of economics that specifically dealt with land usage . It focused on maximizing the crop yield while maintaining a good soil ecosystem .  Throughout the 20th century the discipline expanded and the current scope of the discipline is much broader. Agricultural economics today includes a variety of applied areas, having considerable overlap with conventional economics. [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] [ 4 ] Agricultural economists have made substantial contributions to research in economics, econometrics , development economics , and environmental economics .  Agricultural economics influences food policy , agricultural policy , and environmental policy .
